tagline: Through the grass-covered dunes from Alliance to Grand Island.
intro: East of Alliance, Highway 2 goes into the Sand Hills, mixed-grass prairie laid over dunes that can stand more than 330 feet high, most of it never plowed. Shallow lakes sit in the low ground between the dunes. The towns, Ellsworth, Hyannis, Mullen, Thedford and Halsey, all date from 1887 and 1888, when the railroad came through. At Dunning the road turns southeast for Broken Bow, Ravenna and Grand Island.
In spring the sandhill cranes pass over. Near Halsey stands Charles Bessey's answer to whether a forest could be grown where there was none.

moments.title: Ellsworth
moments.text: Cattleman Bartlett Richards made this railroad water stop the company town of his Spade Ranch, and its two-story store of 1898 supplied the freight wagons heading north to headquarters.

moments.title: Nebraska National Forest, Bessey District
moments.text: Begun in 1902 as an experiment in growing timber on treeless sand hills, the planting reached 20,000 acres, the largest human-planted forest in the United States.

moments.title: Broken Bow
moments.text: The name most likely came from a settler who found a broken bow in a field where there had been a Native American camp.
